If you're still on the fence about upgrading to macOS 27 Golden Gate, the massive pile of security patches Apple just dropped might be enough to convince you. And if you plan to stick with an older version, you should install macOS Tahoe 26.7 or macOS Sequoia 15.7 as soon as possible. Here's why.

Apple Patches Over 200 macOS Vulnerabilities

Apple today published the full security release notes for macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8, detailing the more than 200 vulnerabilities fixed in these updates.

As with several recent macOS updates, Apple called out a number of AI-related security teams and researchers in its acknowledgments, including OpenAI Codex Security, NVIDIA AI Red Team, and Anthropic Research.

The patches in macOS 27 span numerous categories of vulnerabilities that could be exploited by malicious apps or attackers to execute arbitrary code with kernel or root privileges, escape the macOS sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper, modify protected system files, access sensitive user data, and more.

For example, an AVEVideoEncoder vulnerability could allow a sandboxed app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges, and a UDF file system vulnerability could similarly allow an app to execute code at the kernel level. Apple also patched vulnerabilities that could lead to remote code execution via Bluetooth, CUPS, and WebDAV.

As for macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8, both address many of the above vulnerabilities, including multiple kernel-level, root privilege, sandbox escape, Gatekeeper bypass, and remote code execution issues.

These legacy releases also include some additional fixes not listed under macOS 27, including an ImageIO vulnerability in macOS Sequoia 15.8 that could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted image.

  • About the security content of macOS Tahoe 26.7
  • About the security content of macOS Sequoia 15.8

Will you upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate or stick with macOS Tahoe 26? Let us know in the comments.
